extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, peer reviewers, and researchers studying peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Applying a five-dimension manuscript-evaluation rubric (JABA form) to rate journal submissions on topic relevance, methodology, data presentation, discussion, and overall contribution, using 4-point component and recommendation scales plus open-ended justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance and pertinence of the research question to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Soundness of experimental procedures, controls, and design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers were instructed to evaluate the methods independently, but Mahoney's findings show an anti-pattern: identical methods sections were rated higher when results agreed with reviewers' priors (i.e., outcome can bias perceived methodological quality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity, accuracy, and adequacy of how findings are reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of interpretation, scope of inference, treatment of alternative explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall scientific contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Net advance the manuscript would represent for the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Component rating scale (per-dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 4-point ordinal rating scale used for each component: Poor; Marginal; Adequate; Good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For statistical analysis the four categories were re-expressed on a 0/2/4/6 Likert metric (0 = lowest, 6 = highest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary recommendation scale
rubrics_metrics.description: A separate 4-point editorial recommendation scale: Accept; Accept with minor revisions; Accept with major revisions; Reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recommendation is recorded separately from the component ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-ended referee form
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative justifications supplied by reviewers for each component rating and the overall recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers were instructed to use the evaluation criteria explicitly outlined by JABA when supplying narrative justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate methodological evaluation from outcome evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should separate methodological evaluation from outcome evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mahoney showed identical methods sections were rated higher when results agreed with reviewers' priors — practitioners should avoid letting outcome direction influence assessment of methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid confirmatory bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should avoid confirmatory bias: judging the truth of a finding by whether it conforms to the reviewer's theoretical commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit prescriptive norm derived from Mahoney's experimental findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mask identities and outcome direction during methodological appraisal
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should mask reviewer identities and where possible mask outcome direction during methodological appraisal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mahoney's results motivate procedural steps (e.g., blinding) to reduce bias in methodological evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag theoretical priors
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should explicitly flag their own theoretical priors that might bias appraisal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declaring priors helps make potential biases visible and can mitigate confirmatory evaluation.
